summary: Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He was dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1934–1945) and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1946–1949).

Donna C. Kurtz is a history and archaeology scholar. She studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College, and held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre from circa 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1995) and served on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology and related fields. She earned her doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned a BA at Hunter College and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. She curated at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art (~1987–1993) and is a Research Scholar at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).
Doris Unterthurner is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen.
Dorje Tseten was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948). He served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium, the école militaire russo-mongole, and Kazan University, completing a doctoral dissertation under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (~1842–1846).

Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She was a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and affiliate faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Dosho Port is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied under traditional teachers Dainin Katagiri, Toni Packer, Thich Nhat Hanh, Tangen Harada, Shodo Harada, John Daido Loori, and James Ishmael Ford.

Douglas Allen is a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Yale, Banaras Hindu University, and Vanderbilt. He held teaching posts at Southern Illinois, Central Connecticut State, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus of Philosophy in 2020.

Douglas Duckworth is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He has held teaching posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University (~2011–2014).

Douglas Fairchild Ober is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 2016) under Harjot Oberoi.
Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Princeton University, where he studied under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.
Douglas J. Penick is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University (~1962–1966) and studied under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He taught philosophy at Southern Illinois University (attested 2007–2014) and serves as Professor and Director of the Centre for Intercultural Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Douglas Osto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He held posts at Massey University starting in 2005, becoming Senior Lecturer in ~2007.

Douglas Q. Adams is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (through 1972) and held a post at the University of Idaho circa 1972.
Dragana Majhen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).
